title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 2. Absorption in the Boar
html:
The Lord's ecstasy at the sound of a flute; kirtanas in Srivasa's house; a heavenly voice consoles the Lord; in Murari's house He takes on the form of the Boar and speaks of Himself and the Vedas; His explanation of the verse on the holy name

Verse 1

श्रीवासपण्डितैः सार्धं तद्भ्रातृभिरलंकृतैः।
गच्छन्पथि हरिर्वंशीनादश्रवणविह्वलः॥१॥

śrīvāsapaṇḍitaiḥ sārdhaṁ tadbhrātṛbhiralaṁkṛtaiḥ|
gacchanpathi harirvaṁśīnādaśravaṇavihvalaḥ||1||

shrivasa-panditaih sardham — together with Srivasa Pandita; tat-bhratribhih — with his brothers; alankritaih — adorned; gachchhan — going; pathi — on the road; harih — Hari; vamshi-nada-shravana-vihvalah — overwhelmed on hearing the sound of a flute.

1Once, while walking along the road with Srivasa Pandita, who was adorned by his brothers, Hari heard the sound of a flute and was overwhelmed.

Verse 2

पपात दण्डवद्भूमौ मोहितोऽभूत्क्षणं पुनः।
रौति नानाविधं देवस्त्वचिरेण विबुध्यते॥२॥

papāta daṇḍavadbhūmau mohito'bhūtkṣaṇaṁ punaḥ|
rauti nānāvidhaṁ devastvacireṇa vibudhyate||2||

papata — fell; dandavat — like a stick; bhumau — to the ground; mohitah — senseless; abhut — was; kshanam — for a moment; punah — then; rauti — cries; nana-vidham — in various ways; devah — the Lord; tu — and; achirena — soon; vibudhyate — comes to Himself.

2He fell to the ground like a stick and for a moment lost consciousness; then He cried out in various ways, but soon came to Himself.

Verse 3

आशीर्युञ्जन्द्विजाग्र्येषु प्रहसन्रुचिराननः।
शिष्टैरुपेतो मुमुदे कदाचिल्लौकिकीं क्रियाम्॥३॥

āśīryuñjandvijāgryeṣu prahasanrucirānanaḥ|
śiṣṭairupeto mumude kadācillaukikīṁ kriyām||3||

ashir-yunjan — bestowing blessings; dvija-agryeshu — on the foremost brahmanas; prahasan — laughing; ruchira-ananah — with lovely face; shishtaih — by worthy people; upetah — surrounded; mumude — rejoiced; kadachit — sometimes; laukikim — worldly; kriyam — acts.

3At times, blessing the foremost brahmanas, laughing, His face radiant with beauty, He rejoiced in the company of worthy people; and at times the Lord of Kamala1

Verse 4

करोति कमलाध्यक्षो देहयात्राप्रसिद्धये।
नवद्वीपविलासं च दर्शयन्जगतीपतिः॥४॥

karoti kamalādhyakṣo dehayātrāprasiddhaye|
navadvīpavilāsaṁ ca darśayanjagatīpatiḥ||4||

karoti — performs; kamala-adhyakshah — the Lord of Kamala; deha-yatra-prasiddhaye — for the maintenance of the body; navadvipa-vilasam — the Navadvipa pastimes; cha — and; darshayan — displaying; jagati-patih — the Lord of the earth.

4also performed the ordinary acts of daily life needed to maintain the body, displaying His pastimes in Navadvipa — He, the Lord of the earth.

Verse 5

श्रीवासपण्डितैः सार्धं श्रीरामेण महात्मना।
तयोः पुर्यां मुकुन्देन वैद्येनान्येन स प्रभुः॥५॥

śrīvāsapaṇḍitaiḥ sārdhaṁ śrīrāmeṇa mahātmanā|
tayoḥ puryāṁ mukundena vaidyenānyena sa prabhuḥ||5||

shrivasa-panditaih sardham — with Srivasa Pandita; shri-ramena — with Sri Rama; mahatmana — great-souled; tayoh — of the two; puryam — in the house; mukundena — with Mukunda; vaidyena — with a vaidya; anyena — with another; sah — that; prabhuh — Lord.

5With Srivasa Pandita and the great-souled Sri Rama2, in their house, with Mukunda and another vaidya3, the Lord

Verse 6

ननर्त च जगौ कृष्णगीतं हरिपरायणैः।
रात्रौ रात्रौ दिवा प्रेम्णा पुलकाञ्चितविग्रहः॥६॥

nanarta ca jagau kṛṣṇagītaṁ hariparāyaṇaiḥ|
rātrau rātrau divā premṇā pulakāñcitavigrahaḥ||6||

nanarta — danced; cha — and; jagau — sang; krishna-gitam — songs of Krishna; hari-parayanaih — with those devoted to Hari; ratrau ratrau — night after night; diva — by day; premna — with love; pulaka-anchita-vigrahah — His body thrilled with gooseflesh.

6danced and sang songs of Krishna together with those devoted to Hari — night after night, and by day as well — His body thrilling with love.

Verse 7

एकदा निजगेहे स वसन्प्रेमातिविह्वलः।
वसामि कुत्र तिष्ठामि कथं मे स्यान्मतिर्हरौ॥७॥

ekadā nijagehe sa vasanpremātivihvalaḥ|
vasāmi kutra tiṣṭhāmi kathaṁ me syānmatirharau||7||

ekada — once; nija-gehe — in His own house; sah — He; vasan — staying; prema-ati-vihvalah — utterly overwhelmed by love; vasami — I live; kutra — where; tishthami — I stay; katham — how; me — My; syat — may be; matih — mind; harau — on Hari.

7Once, while staying at home, utterly overwhelmed by love, He (cried): "Where am I to live, where am I to stay? How can My mind be fixed on Hari?"

Verse 8

इति विह्वलितं देवो नाम्ना तं प्राह सादरम्।
हरेरंशमवेहि त्वमात्मानं पृथिवीतले॥८॥

iti vihvalitaṁ devo nāmnā taṁ prāha sādaram|
hareraṁśamavehi tvamātmānaṁ pṛthivītale||8||

iti — thus; vihvalitam — to the overwhelmed one; devah — a deity; namna — by name; tam — to Him; praha — spoke; sadaram — respectfully; hareh — of Hari; amsham — a portion; avehi — know; tvam — You; atmanam — Yourself; prithivi-tale — on the earth.

8Then a deity, calling Him respectfully by name, addressed Him in that overwhelmed state: "Know Yourself to be a portion of Hari on earth4.

Verse 9

अवतीर्णोऽसि भगवन्लोकानां प्रेमसिद्धये।
खेदं मा कुरु यज्ञोऽयं कीर्तनाख्यः क्षितौ कलौ॥९॥

avatīrṇo'si bhagavanlokānāṁ premasiddhaye|
khedaṁ mā kuru yajño'yaṁ kīrtanākhyaḥ kṣitau kalau||9||

avatirnah asi — You have descended; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; lokanam — for the people; prema-siddhaye — for the attainment of love; khedam — sorrow; ma kuru — do not indulge in; yajnah — sacrifice; ayam — this; kirtana-akhyah — called kirtana; kshitau — on earth; kalau — in Kali.

9You have descended, O Bhagavan, so that people may attain love. Do not grieve: this sacrifice called kirtana, on earth in the age of Kali,

Verse 10

त्वत्प्रसादात्सुसम्पन्नो भविष्यति न संशयः।
एवं श्रुत्वा गिरं देव्या हर्षयुक्तो बभूव सः॥१०॥

tvatprasādātsusampanno bhaviṣyati na saṁśayaḥ|
evaṁ śrutvā giraṁ devyā harṣayukto babhūva saḥ||10||

tvat-prasadat — by Your grace; susampannah — fully accomplished; bhavishyati — will be; na samshayah — no doubt; evam — thus; shrutva — having heard; giram — the speech; devyah — of the divine voice; harsha-yuktah — joyful; babhuva — became; sah — He.

10will be fully accomplished by Your grace — of this there is no doubt." Hearing these words of the divine voice, He was filled with joy.

Verse 11

कदाचिद्दैवयोगेन हरिर्दीनानुकम्पया।
ययौ वैद्यमुरारेः स वाट्यां प्रेमार्द्रलोचनः॥११॥

kadāciddaivayogena harirdīnānukampayā|
yayau vaidyamurāreḥ sa vāṭyāṁ premārdralocanaḥ||11||

kadachit — once; daiva-yogena — by providence; harih — Hari; dina-anukampaya — out of compassion for the lowly; yayau — went; vaidya-murareh — of the vaidya Murari; sah — He; vatyam — to the house; prema-ardra-lochanah — His eyes moist with love.

11Once, by providence, Hari, out of compassion for the lowly, came to the house of the vaidya Murari, His eyes moist with love.

Verse 12

देवतागृहमध्ये संप्रविश्योपाविशद्विभुः।
आप्लुतः प्रेमधाराभिर्निर्झरैरिव पर्वतः॥१२॥

devatāgṛhamadhye saṁpraviśyopāviśadvibhuḥ|
āplutaḥ premadhārābhirnirjharairiva parvataḥ||12||

devata-griha-madhye — into the shrine-room; sampravishya — having entered; upavishat — sat down; vibhuh — the Almighty; aplutah — bathed; prema-dharabhih — by streams of love; nirjharaih — by waterfalls; iva — like; parvatah — a mountain.

12Entering the shrine-room, the Almighty sat down, bathed in streams of love like a mountain in waterfalls.

Verse 13

अहो मां दन्तयुग्मेन तुदत्येष महाबलः।
वराहः पर्वताकार इत्युक्त्वापसरन्क्रमात्॥१३॥

aho māṁ dantayugmena tudatyeṣa mahābalaḥ|
varāhaḥ parvatākāra ityuktvāpasarankramāt||13||

aho — ah!; mam — Me; danta-yugmena — with a pair of tusks; tudati — gores; eshah — this; maha-balah — mighty; varahah — boar; parvata-akarah — the size of a mountain; iti — thus; uktva — having said; apasaran — retreating; kramat — step by step.

13"Ah! This mighty boar, huge as a mountain, is goring Me with his two tusks!" He said, and step by step He began to back away.

Verse 14

अहो मां हि तुदत्येष दशनैः शूकरोत्तमः।
इत्युक्त्वापससाराशु पुनरेव महाप्रभुः॥१४॥

aho māṁ hi tudatyeṣa daśanaiḥ śūkarottamaḥ|
ityuktvāpasasārāśu punareva mahāprabhuḥ||14||

aho — ah!; mam — Me; hi — indeed; tudati — gores; eshah — this; dashanaih — with his tusks; shukara-uttamah — best of boars; iti — thus; uktva — having said; apasasara — retreated; ashu — quickly; punah eva — again; maha-prabhuh — Mahaprabhu.

14"Ah! This best of boars is goring Me with his tusks!" Mahaprabhu said again, and quickly retreated.

Verse 15

ततः क्षणेनेश्वरत्वं भावेन दर्शयन्स्वयम्।
जानुभ्यां भूमिमालम्ब्य करयुग्मेन स व्रजन्॥१५॥

tataḥ kṣaṇeneśvaratvaṁ bhāvena darśayansvayam|
jānubhyāṁ bhūmimālambya karayugmena sa vrajan||15||

tatah — then; kshanena — in a moment; ishvaratvam — His lordship; bhavena — in ecstasy; darshayan — displaying; svayam — Himself; janubhyam — with the knees; bhumim — on the ground; alambya — resting; kara-yugmena — with both hands; sah — He; vrajan — moving.

15Then, a moment later, Himself revealing in ecstasy His nature as the Lord, He went on all fours, resting His knees and both hands on the ground,

Verse 16

वर्तुलाम्बुजनेत्रेण हुङ्कारेणानुनादयन्।
दधार दशनाग्रेण पैत्तलं जलपात्रकम्॥१६॥

vartulāmbujanetreṇa huṅkāreṇānunādayan|
dadhāra daśanāgreṇa paittalaṁ jalapātrakam||16||

vartula-ambuja-netrena — with round lotus eyes; hunkarena — with a roar; anunadayan — making (all) resound; dadhara — lifted; dashana-agrena — with the tips of His tusks; paittalam — a brass; jala-patrakam — water-pot.

16and, rolling His round lotus eyes and making all resound with His roar, He lifted a brass water-pot on the tips of His tusks.

Verse 17

क्षणमुन्मुखतां कृत्वा पश्चाद्धृत्वा तु पैत्तलम्।
पात्रमूचे स्वरूपं मे वदस्वेति मुरारिकम्॥१७॥

kṣaṇamunmukhatāṁ kṛtvā paścāddhṛtvā tu paittalam|
pātramūce svarūpaṁ me vadasveti murārikam||17||

kshanam — for a moment; unmukhatam — upturned face; kritva — making; pashchat — afterwards; dhritva — holding; tu — and; paittalam — the brass; patram — pot; uche — said; svarupam — true form; me — My; vadasva — describe; iti — thus; murarikam — to (humble) Murari.

17For a moment He turned His face upward; then, holding the brass pot, He said to humble Murari: "Describe My true form."

Verse 18

स प्रोवाच नमन्भूमौ विस्मितो दृश्य ईश्वरः।
नाहं वेद्मि स्वरूपं ते भगवन्वनजेक्षण॥१८॥

sa provāca namanbhūmau vismito dṛśya īśvaraḥ|
nāhaṁ vedmi svarūpaṁ te bhagavanvanajekṣaṇa||18||

sah — he; provacha — said; naman — bowing; bhumau — to the ground; vismitah — astonished; drishyah — visible; ishvarah — the Lord; na — not; aham — I; vedmi — know; svarupam — true form; te — Your; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; vanaja-ikshana — O lotus-eyed one.

18Astonished, he bowed to the ground and said: "You are the Lord made visible; but Your true form I do not know, O Bhagavan, O lotus-eyed one.

Verse 19

स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम।
इति गीतोक्तवचसा वदन्तं स पुनः पुनः॥१९॥

svayamevātmanātmānaṁ vettha tvaṁ puruṣottama|
iti gītoktavacasā vadantaṁ sa punaḥ punaḥ||19||

svayam eva — Yourself alone; atmana — by Yourself; atmanam — Yourself; vettha — know; tvam — You; purushottama — O Supreme Person; iti — thus; gita-ukta-vachasa — with the words spoken in the Gita; vadantam — to him who was saying; sah — He; punah punah — again and again.

19You alone know Yourself by Yourself, O Supreme Person5." And as he kept repeating these words of the Gita,

Verse 20

ततस्तं भगवान्प्राह पुनः सुश्लक्ष्णया गिरा।
किं मां जानाति वेदोऽयं वैद्यः प्राह स तं प्रभुम्॥२०॥

tatastaṁ bhagavānprāha punaḥ suślakṣṇayā girā|
kiṁ māṁ jānāti vedo'yaṁ vaidyaḥ prāha sa taṁ prabhum||20||

tatah — then; tam — to him; bhagavan — Bhagavan; praha — said; punah — again; sushlakshnaya — very gentle; gira — in a voice; kim — does; mam — Me; janati — know; vedah — Veda; ayam — this; vaidyah — the vaidya; praha — said; sah — he; tam — to that; prabhum — Lord.

20Bhagavan again asked him in a very gentle voice: "And does the Veda know Me?" The vaidya answered the Lord:

Verse 21

वेदस्य शक्तिर्नास्ति त्वां वक्तुं गुह्योऽसि सर्वदा।
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्प्राह वेदो विडम्बयत्यलम्॥२१॥

vedasya śaktirnāsti tvāṁ vaktuṁ guhyo'si sarvadā|
tacchrutvā bhagavānprāha vedo viḍambayatyalam||21||

vedasya — of the Veda; shaktih — the power; na asti — there is not; tvam — You; vaktum — to describe; guhyah — hidden; asi — You are; sarvada — always; tat — that; shrutva — having heard; bhagavan — Bhagavan; praha — said; vedah — the Veda; vidambayati — mocks; alam — thoroughly.

21"The Veda has no power to describe You: You are ever hidden." Hearing this, Bhagavan said: "The Veda mocks Me thoroughly:

Verse 22

मां वक्त्यपाणिपादेति वदन्स्मृत्वाब्रवीदिदम्।
भगवान्वेदसारज्ञः सर्ववेदार्थनिर्मितः॥२२॥

māṁ vaktyapāṇipādeti vadansmṛtvābravīdidam|
bhagavānvedasārajñaḥ sarvavedārthanirmitaḥ||22||

mam — Me; vakti — calls; apani-pada — without hands and feet; iti — thus; vadan — saying; smritva — recalling; abravit — recited; idam — this; bhagavan — Bhagavan; veda-sara-jnah — knower of the essence of the Vedas; sarva-veda-artha-nirmitah — fashioned of the meaning of all the Vedas.

22it calls Me handless and footless." With these words Bhagavan, knower of the essence of the Vedas, fashioned of the meaning of all the Vedas, recalled and recited this verse:

Verse 23

अपाणिपादो जवनो ग्रहीता
पश्यत्यचक्षुः स शृणोत्यकर्णः।
स वेत्ति विश्वं नहि तस्य वेत्ता
तमाहुरग्र्यं पुरुषं पुराणम्॥२३॥

apāṇipādo javano grahītā
paśyatyacakṣuḥ sa śṛṇotyakarṇaḥ|
sa vetti viśvaṁ nahi tasya vettā
tamāhuragryaṁ puruṣaṁ purāṇam||23||

apani-padah — without hands and feet; javanah — swift; grahita — grasping; pashyati — sees; achakshuh — eyeless; sah — He; shrinoti — hears; akarnah — earless; sah — He; vetti — knows; vishvam — the universe; na hi — but not; tasya — of Him; vetta — a knower; tam — Him; ahuh — they call; agryam — the foremost; purusham — Person; puranam — primeval.

23"Without hands and feet, He is swift and grasps; without eyes He sees, without ears He hears; He knows the universe, but no one knows Him; Him they call the foremost, primeval Person6."

Verse 24

इति वेदवचो देवो हसन्नेवाभ्यभाषत।
नहि जानाति वेदो मामिति निश्चितमेव हि॥२४॥

iti vedavaco devo hasannevābhyabhāṣata|
nahi jānāti vedo māmiti niścitameva hi||24||

iti — thus; veda-vachah — the words of the Veda; devah — the Lord; hasan eva — laughing; abhyabhashata — recited; na hi — not at all; janati — knows; vedah — the Veda; mam — Me; iti — thus; nishchitam — certain; eva hi — indeed.

24Having recited these words of the Veda with a laugh, the Lord said: "The Veda does not know Me at all — that is certain."

Verse 25

अम्बष्ठः प्राह भगवन्करुणां कर्तुमर्हसि।
तं प्राह भगवान्देवः प्रेमा मयि दयामयः॥२५॥

ambaṣṭhaḥ prāha bhagavankaruṇāṁ kartumarhasi|
taṁ prāha bhagavāndevaḥ premā mayi dayāmayaḥ||25||

ambashthah — the Ambashtha; praha — said; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; karunam — mercy; kartum arhasi — please show; tam — to him; praha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; devah — the Lord; prema — love; mayi — for Me; daya-mayah — the merciful.

25The Ambashtha7 said: "O Bhagavan, be merciful to me!" The merciful Bhagavan answered him: "(May you have) love for Me."

Verse 26

इत्युक्त्वा स स्मितमुखो जगाम निजमन्दिरम्।
श्रीमान्विश्वम्भरो देवो हरिकीर्तनतत्परः॥२६॥

ityuktvā sa smitamukho jagāma nijamandiram|
śrīmānviśvambharo devo harikīrtanatatparaḥ||26||

iti — thus; uktva — having said; sah — He; smita-mukhah — with a smiling face; jagama — went; nija-mandiram — to His own house; shriman — the beautiful; vishvambharah — Vishvambhara; devah — the Lord; hari-kirtana-tatparah — devoted to Hari's kirtana.

26Having said this, the beautiful Lord Vishvambhara, devoted to Hari's kirtana, went home with a smile.

Verse 27

अपरेद्युः पण्डितस्य श्रीवासस्य पुरे वसन्।
व्याख्यां चकार श्लोकस्य वक्ष्यमाणस्य तच्छृणु॥२७॥

aparedyuḥ paṇḍitasya śrīvāsasya pure vasan|
vyākhyāṁ cakāra ślokasya vakṣyamāṇasya tacchṛṇu||27||

aparedyuh — the next day; panditasya — of the Pandita; shrivasasya — Srivasa; pure — in the house; vasan — staying; vyakhyam — an explanation; chakara — gave; shlokasya — of the verse; vakshyamanasya — to be cited; tat — that; shrinu — hear.

27The next day, while at the house of Srivasa Pandita, He explained a verse which I shall now quote — listen:

Verse 28

हरेर्नाम हरेर्नाम हरेर्नामैव केवलम्।
कलौ नास्त्येव नास्त्येव नास्त्येव गतिरन्यथा॥२८॥

harernāma harernāma harernāmaiva kevalam|
kalau nāstyeva nāstyeva nāstyeva gatiranyathā||28||

hareh nama — the name of Hari; hareh nama — the name of Hari; hareh nama eva — the name of Hari alone; kevalam — solely; kalau — in Kali; na asti eva — there is none; na asti eva — there is none; na asti eva — there is none; gatih — way; anyatha — other.

28"The name of Hari, the name of Hari, the name of Hari alone is the only one! In Kali there is no, no, no other way8."

Verse 29

ना पुमानादिपुरुषः कलावस्त्येव रूपवान्।
नामस्वरूपिणं तं तु जानीहि स तु केवलम्॥२९॥

nā pumānādipuruṣaḥ kalāvastyeva rūpavān|
nāmasvarūpiṇaṁ taṁ tu jānīhi sa tu kevalam||29||

na — "na" (person); puman — a man; adi-purushah — the Original Person; kalau — in Kali; asti eva — is present indeed; rupavan — possessing form; nama-svarupinam — as having the Name for His form; tam — Him; tu — and; janihi — know; sah — He; tu — and; kevalam — "alone."

29"'Na' is the man, the Original Person, who in Kali is present possessing form. Know, then, that His form is the Name; He is the 'only one'9.

Verse 30

वारत्रयं हरेर्नाम दृढार्थं सर्वदेहिनाम्।
एवकारश्च जीवानां पापानां नाशहेतवे॥३०॥

vāratrayaṁ harernāma dṛḍhārthaṁ sarvadehinām|
evakāraśca jīvānāṁ pāpānāṁ nāśahetave||30||

vara-trayam — three times; hareh nama — "the name of Hari"; dridha-artham — for confirmation; sarva-dehinam — for all embodied beings; eva-karah — the word "eva"; cha — and; jivanam — of living beings; papanam — of the sins; nasha-hetave — for the destruction.

30Three times 'the name of Hari' — to confirm (the truth) for all embodied beings; and the word 'eva' ('alone') — to destroy the sins of living beings.

Verse 31

सर्वतत्त्वप्रकाशार्थं केवलं मन्यते च हि।
प्रारब्धकर्मनिर्वाणं कथ्यतेऽद्वैतवादिभिः॥३१॥

sarvatattvaprakāśārthaṁ kevalaṁ manyate ca hi|
prārabdhakarmanirvāṇaṁ kathyate'dvaitavādibhiḥ||31||

sarva-tattva-prakasha-artham — as revealing all truths; kevalam — "kevalam"; manyate — is understood; cha hi — indeed; prarabdha-karma-nirvanam — the extinction of karma already bearing fruit; kathyate — is said; advaita-vadibhih — by the proponents of non-duality.

31'The only one' is understood as revealing all truths; whereas the proponents of non-duality say it is the extinction of karma already bearing fruit.

Verse 32

भवेदिति च बोधार्थं कैवल्यं केवलं स्मृतम्।
कृष्णप्रेमरसास्वादप्रापकं करुणामयम्॥३२॥

bhavediti ca bodhārthaṁ kaivalyaṁ kevalaṁ smṛtam|
kṛṣṇapremarasāsvādaprāpakaṁ karuṇāmayam||32||

bhavet — "may it be"; iti — thus; cha — and; bodha-artham — in order to understand; kaivalyam — "kaivalya"; kevalam — "kevalam"; smritam — is held to be; krishna-prema-rasa-asvada-prapakam — bestowing the taste of the rasa of love for Krishna; karuna-mayam — full of mercy.

32Supplying 'may it be,' they take 'the only one' to mean liberation, kaivalya; but (the Name) is full of mercy and bestows the taste of the rasa of love for Krishna.

Verse 33

तत्स्वरूपं हरेर्नाम योऽन्यदेव वदेत्पुमान्।
तस्य नास्त्येव नास्त्येव गतिरित्यवदत्स्वयम्॥३३॥

tatsvarūpaṁ harernāma yo'nyadeva vadetpumān|
tasya nāstyeva nāstyeva gatirityavadatsvayam||33||

tat-svarupam — His very form; hareh nama — the name of Hari; yah — who; anyat eva — otherwise; vadet — says; puman — a man; tasya — for him; na asti eva — there is none; na asti eva — there is none; gatih — way; iti — thus; avadat — said; svayam — Himself.

33The name of Hari is His very form. Whoever says otherwise has no, no way," — so He Himself said.

Verse 34

इत्यसौ शूकरो ब्रूते सर्वदेवमयः पुमान्।
इत्युक्त्वा नर्तनं चक्रे कीर्तनं च विशेषतः॥३४॥

ityasau śūkaro brūte sarvadevamayaḥ pumān|
ityuktvā nartanaṁ cakre kīrtanaṁ ca viśeṣataḥ||34||

iti — thus; asau — this; shukarah — Boar; brute — says; sarva-deva-mayah — comprising all the gods; puman — the Person; iti — thus; uktva — having said; nartanam — dance; chakre — performed; kirtanam — kirtana; cha — and; visheshatah — especially.

34"So says this Boar, the Person who comprises all the gods" — having said this, He began to dance, and above all to sing kirtana.

Verse 35

एतद्यः शृणुयान्नित्यं कीर्तयेद्वा समाहितः।
हरौ प्रेमा भवेत्तस्य विपाप्मा च भवेद्ध्रुवम्॥३५॥

etadyaḥ śṛṇuyānnityaṁ kīrtayedvā samāhitaḥ|
harau premā bhavettasya vipāpmā ca bhaveddhruvam||35||

etat — this; yah — who; shrinuyat — hears; nityam — constantly; kirtayet — recounts; va — or; samahitah — attentively; harau — for Hari; prema — love; bhavet — will be; tasya — his; vipapma — sinless; cha — and; bhavet — will become; dhruvam — surely.

35Whoever constantly and attentively hears or recounts this will surely come to love Hari and will become free from sin;

Verse 36

श्रीमच्चैतन्यपादाब्जे प्रभुबुद्धिर्दृढा भवेत्।
अन्ते चैतन्यदेवस्य स्मृतिर्भवति शाश्वती॥३६॥

śrīmaccaitanyapādābje prabhubuddhirdṛḍhā bhavet|
ante caitanyadevasya smṛtirbhavati śāśvatī||36||

shrimach-chaitanya-pada-abje — at the lotus feet of Sri Chaitanya; prabhu-buddhih — the awareness (of Him) as Lord; dridha — firm; bhavet — will be; ante — at the end; chaitanya-devasya — of Chaitanya-deva; smritih — remembrance; bhavati — comes; shashvati — unfailing.

36at the lotus feet of Sri Chaitanya his awareness that He is the Lord will become firm, and at the end of life unfailing remembrance of Chaitanya-deva will come to him.

Thus ends the second sarga, "Absorption in the Boar" (Varaha-avesha), in the description of Chaitanya's descent, of the second prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Kamala is Lakshmi, the consort of Vishnu.
  2. Sri Rama (Ramai Pandita) was Srivasa's younger brother.
  3. A vaidya is a member of the physician caste. Mukunda Datta was a vaidya; "another vaidya" is apparently the author himself, Murari Gupta.
  4. Here the Lord is in the mood of a devotee longing for Hari (v. 7), and the voice from above answers Him in keeping with that mood. "Portion" (amsha) does not diminish Him: the same voice calls Him Bhagavan, descended to bestow love (v. 9), and immediately afterwards He Himself reveals His nature as the Lord (v. 15). For Gaudiya Vaishnavas Sri Chaitanya is Krishna Himself in the mood of Radha (cf. 1.04, the note to v. 26).
  5. Bhagavad-gita 10.15.
  6. Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.19 (as the poem reads it). "Without hands and feet" here means without material hands and feet; the Lord's hands and feet are spiritual, and that is why He is "swift" and "grasps." So the Lord, having appeared as the Boar, laughs at the Veda for seemingly calling Him handless and footless: it has no power to describe Him directly (vv. 21, 24).
  7. Ambashtha is the name of the vaidya caste; here, Murari.
  8. A verse of the Brihan-naradiya Purana. In verses 29–33 the Lord comments on its words.
  9. "Na" (nā) means "man, person"; the explanation apparently plays on the beginning of the word nama ("name"). The sense of verses 29–32 is unclear in places; the translation is tentative.
